title: REST API patterns (any service)
summary: Every common REST scenario: lists, pagination, filters, items, caching, writes, bulk, uploads, content negotiation, error handling and auth. Includes an enterprise test plan (jobs starting ent-).
description: Covers every common REST scenario for any JSON API: lists, pagination (first page and deep offset), filtering, sorting, sparse fields and expanded relations, single and missing items, conditional requests, create, replace, patch and delete, bulk and large bodies, uploads, content negotiation, error handling and authentication.

variables.name: url
variables.description: API base URL, no trailing slash
variables.guide: The address of the system to test, starting with https:// (or http://) and with no trailing slash, for example https://staging.example.com. Use a system you own, ideally a staging copy. BLASTA runs in a container, so for a service on your own machine use host.docker.internal instead of localhost.

variables.name: resource
variables.guide: The path of a collection in the API, starting with /, for example /api/v1/items. Look in the API documentation or its OpenAPI file.

variables.name: id
variables.guide: The ID of an existing record, as it appears in the API or the address, for example 1.

variables.name: uploadPath
variables.guide: The path of a file upload endpoint, starting with /, from the API documentation.

variables.name: token
variables.description: Bearer token. Read from API_TOKEN by the CLI.

jobs.name: list collection
jobs.notes: The most common call. If it is slow with no filters, look at default page size and missing indexes.

jobs.name: pagination: first page
jobs.notes: Cursor or offset page 1.

jobs.name: pagination: deep offset
jobs.notes: OFFSET 10000 forces the database to skip 10,000 rows per request, so latency grows with the page number. Compare with the first page; if it is slower, move to cursor (keyset) pagination.

jobs.name: filtered list
jobs.notes: Filtering on a column without an index is a table scan: the first thing to check when a list endpoint gets slower as data grows.

jobs.name: sorted list
jobs.notes: Sorting on an unindexed field sorts every matching row in memory.

jobs.name: sparse fields
jobs.notes: Asking for fewer fields should be cheaper. If it costs the same, the API loads everything anyway.

jobs.name: expanded relations
jobs.notes: ?include= or ?expand= triggers extra queries per row (the N+1 problem). Latency that grows with limit gives it away.

jobs.name: get one item
jobs.notes: Primary key lookup: should be the fastest call the API has.

jobs.name: get a missing item
jobs.notes: 404 path: must be as cheap as a hit, and must not leak stack traces.

jobs.name: HEAD item
jobs.notes: Existence check without the body.

jobs.name: OPTIONS (CORS preflight)
jobs.notes: Browsers send this before cross-origin writes; it should never reach the application code.

jobs.name: conditional GET (If-None-Match)
jobs.notes: Sends a deliberately stale ETag. A correct API answers 200 with the new body; a 304 on a wrong ETag would be a caching bug, so only 200 counts.

jobs.name: create an item (POST)
jobs.notes: Write path with validation and an insert. Creates a row per request, so clean up afterwards. Staging only.

jobs.name: retried create (Idempotency-Key)
jobs.notes: Clients retry on timeout. With the same Idempotency-Key the API must create ONE item and replay the response. 409 is also acceptable.

jobs.name: replace an item (PUT)
jobs.notes: Full update of the item named by id. Staging only.

jobs.name: partial update (PATCH)
jobs.notes: Single-field update; row lock contention shows when many requests hit the same id. Staging only.

jobs.name: delete a missing item
jobs.notes: DELETE on an id that does not exist must be a fast 404 (or 204 if idempotent). Never points at a real item.

jobs.name: bulk create (100 items)
jobs.notes: One request carrying 100 rows: tests transaction size, validation loops and the request body limit. Creates 100 rows per request. Staging only.

jobs.name: wrong Content-Type
jobs.notes: A JSON body sent as text/plain must be refused with 415 or 400, not parsed or crash.

jobs.name: malformed JSON body
jobs.notes: Invalid JSON must give a clean 400, quickly, with no stack trace.

jobs.name: unsupported method
jobs.notes: DELETE on the collection must not wipe it: expect 404 or 405.

jobs.name: content negotiation (Accept: XML)
jobs.notes: Asking for a format the API does not offer should be 406 or the default JSON, not an error.

jobs.name: no credentials
jobs.notes: Rejected requests should be cheaper than accepted ones.

jobs.name: OpenAPI document
jobs.notes: Swagger/OpenAPI JSON, fetched by docs and generators; it can be megabytes and is often generated per request.

jobs.name: health endpoint
jobs.notes: Load balancer probe.

jobs.name: read capacity ramp
jobs.notes: Ramps list requests to find the rate where latency climbs.

jobs.name: read soak (10 min)
jobs.notes: Steady load that finds leaks, pool exhaustion and cache decay.

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 01 smoke
jobs.notes: Enterprise plan, step 1 of 10. One request a second for 30 seconds. Run this first, every time: it proves the address, credentials and headers are right and that the environment is up before any real load is applied. Gate: zero errors. Reference request: list collection.

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 02 baseline (20% load)
jobs.notes: Step 2 of 10. About a fifth of normal traffic for 5 minutes: the uncontended latency of this request. Every later result is judged against it, so record p50 and p95. Gate: at most 0.5% errors and the default latency targets. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 02 baseline (20% load)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 03 average load (SLO check)
jobs.notes: Step 3 of 10. Normal busy-hour traffic for 10 minutes. The rate is the reference job's rate: raise it to your measured production peak-hour rate. This is the run that proves (or breaks) your SLO. Gate: at most 1% errors, p95 and p99 inside the targets. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 03 average load (SLO check)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 04 peak load (2x average)
jobs.notes: Step 4 of 10. Twice the average for 10 minutes: the busiest hour of the year plus headroom. Latency may rise, but must stay in SLO; if it does not, you have no headroom. Gate: at most 2% errors, latency targets doubled. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 04 peak load (2x average)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 05 stress (ramp to 4x)
jobs.notes: Step 5 of 10. Ramps to four times average over 10 minutes, then holds for 2. Finds where it degrades and HOW: gracefully (latency rises, errors stay low) or badly (errors, timeouts, crashes, restarts). Observation only, no gate. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 05 stress (ramp to 4x)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 06 spike (10x in 10 s)
jobs.notes: Step 6 of 10. Reaches ten times average within 10 seconds and holds for 2 minutes: a campaign email, a news link, a failover. Checks autoscaling, queue limits and load shedding. Gate: at most 5% errors, because shedding load is acceptable and crashing is not. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 06 spike (10x in 10 s)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 07 recovery after the spike
jobs.notes: Step 7 of 10. Run IMMEDIATELY after the spike, at average load for 5 minutes. Latency and errors must return to the baseline from step 2. If they do not, something is stuck: queues, connection pools, GC, an autoscaler cool-down. Gate: same as average load. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 07 recovery after the spike

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)
jobs.notes: Step 8 of 10. One hour of steady load. Finds leaks and slow decay in memory, connections, file descriptors, disk, log volume and cache churn. Watch the resource graphs: any line that climbs and never flattens is a finding. Gate: at most 0.5% errors. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 08 soak (1 hour at 60%)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)
jobs.notes: Step 9 of 10. Ramps to twenty times average over 20 minutes. Stop it when errors pass about 5%: the rate at that moment is your ceiling, and ceiling divided by peak is your capacity margin. Use a production-like environment, never production. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 09 breakpoint (find the ceiling)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)
jobs.notes: Step 10 of 10. Average load for 15 minutes. About 5 minutes in, cause the event you are testing: kill a pod or node, fail over the database, roll out a new version, drain a zone. Errors in the window are your real availability loss. Gate: at most 1% errors overall; read the time series for how long the dip lasted. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): 10 resilience window (failover / deploy)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): no keep-alive (new connection per request)
jobs.notes: Sends Connection: close, so every request pays for a new TCP and TLS handshake: the cost for clients that do not reuse connections (scripts, some mobile SDKs, health checkers). Shows load balancer and TLS termination limits. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): no keep-alive (new connection per request)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): crawler traffic (Googlebot user agent)
jobs.notes: Same request identified as a search crawler. Tests WAF and bot-management rules and whether crawlers get cached or origin responses. Crawlers can easily be a third of all traffic. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): crawler traffic (Googlebot user agent)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): large cookies (~4 KB header)
jobs.notes: Adds a 4 KB Cookie header, like a logged-in user with many tracking cookies. Proxies and servers reject headers around 8 KB, so this shows how close you are to that limit. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): large cookies (~4 KB header)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): uptime monitors (HEAD from many locations)
jobs.notes: A fleet of synthetic monitors checking the URL with HEAD requests every 30 seconds from 20 locations, plus load balancer probes. Cheap each, constant in total. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): uptime monitors (HEAD from many locations)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): list endpoint peak
jobs.notes: Three times normal for 10 minutes on the most-used endpoint. Reference request: list collection.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): list endpoint peak

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): deep pagination stress
jobs.notes: Ramps requests for page 200 to four times normal. Offset pagination gets slower the deeper you go: a scraper walking the whole collection can take the API down. Reference request: pagination: deep offset.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): deep pagination stress

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): write peak
jobs.notes: Twice normal creates for 10 minutes: an import job or a busy ordering hour. Staging only. Reference request: create an item (POST). This job WRITES or creates data on every request: staging only, and expect a lot of rows.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): write peak

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): hot item (everyone reads the same record)
jobs.notes: Ten times normal concurrency on ONE id: a viral item, a homepage banner, a config record. Exposes row-lock contention, cache stampedes and missing HTTP caching. Reference request: get one item.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): hot item (everyone reads the same record)

jobs.name: REST API patterns (any service): filtered search peak
jobs.notes: Twice normal filtered lists for 10 minutes; unindexed filters are what fall over first. Reference request: filtered list.

job.name: REST API patterns (any service): filtered search peak

API_TOKEN.label: API bearer token
API_TOKEN.guide:
Usually Settings → API tokens (or Personal access tokens) in the service's admin: create a token for testing and copy it.
For an OAuth or OIDC service, request one: `curl -s -d grant_type=client_credentials -d client_id=ID -d client_secret=SECRET https://IDP/token` and copy `access_token`.
Tokens expire (often after 5 to 60 minutes), so create a long-lived one for long runs.
